# Allow @bazel2gn:skip on non-convertible GN targets and skip module-docstring on auto-generated .bzl files

- **Learned from:** inner-loop friction on CL Ib2e9fab824df6ce0bbd2ff226ef41940c510fff5, patchset 2 (task `starnix-line-discipline-pstate`)
- **Date:** 2026-09-28
- **Changed:** `checks/migration_sanity.sh`, `checks/bazel_minimality.sh`

## Root cause

Two deterministic checks contradicted the `target_parity` reviewer rules:

1. `migration_sanity.sh` flagged `# @bazel2gn:skip` as `skipped_convertible_target`
   whenever a target of the same name existed above `## BAZEL2GN SENTINEL` in
   `BUILD.gn`, without checking whether the GN template or Bazel rule is
   convertible by `bazel2gn`. When a non-convertible `genrule` (e.g. invoking an
   interpreter script without a shebang) is paired with a manual `action()` above
   the sentinel, `target_parity` requires `# @bazel2gn:skip`, which
   `migration_sanity.sh` then rejected.
2. `bazel_minimality.sh` ran `buildifier -lint=warn` on all changed `.bzl` files,
   requiring a `module-docstring` even on files generated by tools such as
   `fx update-rustc-third-party` (`# AUTO-GENERATED - DO NOT EDIT!`). Adding a
   manual docstring to satisfy `buildifier` was then rejected by `target_parity`
   for hand-editing an auto-generated file.

## Why not a one-off fix

Any migration that pairs a non-convertible Bazel rule (`genrule`, custom macro)
with a manual GN target above the sentinel, or that runs a code generator
producing `.bzl` files without a module docstring, would hit the same endless
loop between the deterministic check and the reviewer panel. Checking
`CONVERTIBLE_GN_TEMPLATES` / `CONVERTIBLE_BAZEL_RULES` in `migration_sanity.sh`
and skipping `module-docstring` on `AUTO-GENERATED` / `DO NOT EDIT` `.bzl` files
in `bazel_minimality.sh` resolves both classes of false positives across all
future tasks.
